title: Adjective Agreement 5: Chains in 'Это' and 'У меня' Sentences
titleRussian: Согласование прилагательных 5: цепочки в предложениях 'это' и 'у меня'
description: Production practice. Build full sentences with adjective + noun chains in the two highest-frequency A1 frames: 'Это [adj] [noun]' for identification and 'У меня [adj] [noun]' for possession. Mixes hard, soft, and mixed-stem classes from Lessons 1 to 4.
descriptionRussian: Активная практика: составление полных предложений с цепочкой прилагательное + существительное в двух частотных конструкциях — 'Это ___' и 'У меня ___'. Слова из всех трёх классов уроков 1-4.
intro: Everything so far has been a phrase. Now it goes inside a sentence, and specifically inside the two frames a beginner uses more than any others: pointing something out, and saying what you have. Nothing about agreement itself changes when it moves into a frame. What changes is that you have to do it while also thinking about the sentence, which is a different skill and the one that actually breaks down when you speak.
rules: Это is invariant. Whatever the predicate phrase is, masculine or feminine or neuter or plural, это stays это. Agreement happens between the adjective and the noun in the predicate.
У меня + noun keeps the noun in the nominative. The adjective agrees with the noun in the standard nominative way: gender and number from the noun, ending from the adjective's class.

When the sentence goes singular to plural, both the noun and the adjective change. 'Это новый дом' becomes 'Это новые дома': the noun pluralizes (-ы), and the adjective takes the plural ending (-ые / -ие).

Apply the spelling rules from Lesson 4 inside the chain. У Маши хорошие новости (Rule 1: -ие after husher); это большой парк (Rule 3: stressed -ой); это свежее молоко (Rule 2: -ее unstressed after husher).
examples: Это новый дом. (This is a new house.) Hard-stem -ый fits masculine singular дом.
Это красивая улица. (This is a beautiful street.) Hard-stem -ая fits feminine singular улица.
У меня большая семья. (I have a big family.) Stressed-ending -ая (regular feminine) fits feminine singular семья.
У Маши хорошие новости. (Masha has good news.) Mixed-stem plural -ие fits plural новости (Rule 1).
Это синие цветы. (These are blue flowers.) Soft-stem plural -ие fits plural цветы.
У меня новое платье. (I have a new dress.) Hard-stem -ое fits neuter singular платье.

items.hint: Warm-up from Lesson 4. Молоко is neuter singular: which spelling rule shapes the husher-stem ending?
items.explanation: Recall from Lesson 4 (Rule 2): after the husher -ж- with an unstressed ending, write -е not -о. Молоко is neuter singular, so свежее. The 'у Маши' frame does not change the agreement; the chain works the same as in 'Это свежее молоко'.

items.hint: Окно is neuter singular. The hard-stem neuter ending was Lesson 1's plain pattern.
items.explanation: Окно is neuter singular. Hard-stem neuter is -ое, so новое. Это is invariant; agreement happens between the adjective and the noun.

items.hint: Дети is plural. The hard-stem plural ending fits.
items.explanation: Дети is plural. Hard-stem plural is -ые, so умные. The 'у меня' frame keeps the noun in the nominative; the adjective takes the plural form to agree with it.

items.hint: Машина is feminine singular. The soft-stem feminine ending pairs with hard -ая.
items.explanation: Машина is feminine singular. Soft-stem feminine is -яя (Lesson 2), so синяя. The chain inside 'Это ___' carries the same agreement as a stand-alone phrase.

items.hint: Друзья is plural. Lesson 4 Rule 1 shapes the plural ending after a husher.
items.explanation: Друзья is plural. Mixed-stem plural follows Rule 1: after the husher -ш-, write -ие not -ые. So хорошие. The same form works for plural masculine, feminine, and neuter nouns.

items.hint: Стол is masculine singular. After -к-, Lesson 4 Rule 1 shapes the masculine ending.
items.explanation: Стол is masculine singular. Mixed-stem masculine follows Rule 1: after -к-, write -ий not -ый. So маленький. The chain in 'Это маленький стол' is one fluent unit at A1.

items.hint: Дома is plural. Which adjective ending covers all genders in the plural?
items.explanation: Дома is plural, and the plural adjective ending -ые covers all genders: новые дома.

items.hint: Собаки is plural here. Match the adjective.
items.explanation: Собаки is a nominative plural, so the adjective takes the plural -ые: красивые собаки. The 'у меня' frame keeps the noun in the nominative.

items.hint: Окна is plural, and the stem ends in -к.
items.explanation: Окна is plural, so the adjective is plural too, and after -к the spelling rule turns -ые into -ие: высокие окна.

blanks: У меня _____ задание. (I have an interesting assignment.)
fillInBlank.grammarFocus: Задание is neuter singular (-е ending). Hard-stem neuter is -ое: интересное. The 'у меня' frame keeps the noun in the nominative; the chain agrees inside the predicate.

errorCorrection.sentence: Это красивый улица в самом центре города.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: This is a beautiful street in the very centre of the city.
errorCorrection.explanation: Улица is feminine, so the adjective takes the feminine -ая ending: красивая. The 'Это [adj] [noun]' frame is the most common A1 identification structure; agreement happens between the adjective and the noun, not with это (which never changes form).

errorCorrection.sentence: У меня большой семья, шесть человек живут в одном доме.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: I have a big family; six people live in one house.
errorCorrection.explanation: Семья is feminine, so the adjective takes the feminine -ая ending: большая. Большой is masculine (stressed -о́й, the special masculine ending). Note: the spelling rule that produces -ой in the masculine does NOT fire for the feminine; большая follows the regular hard-stem feminine pattern.

errorCorrection.sentence: Это маленький города на юге страны, в горах.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: These are small cities in the south of the country, in the mountains.
errorCorrection.explanation: Города (cities) is plural, so the adjective takes the plural ending. The stem ма́леньк- ends in -к, so Rule 1 (no -ы after -к) forces the plural ending to -ие, not -ые: маленькие. Маленький is masculine singular, so it cannot describe a plural noun. The plural rule is the same across all genders: one form for any plural noun.

minimalPairs.explanation: Суп is masculine singular. After the husher -ч-, Rule 1 produces -ий. So горячий. Горячая would require a feminine noun like горячая чашка.
Книги is plural. The hard-stem plural ending is -ые: новые. Новая is the feminine singular and would need a single feminine book.

reviewVocab.definition: adjective-plus-noun chain (the pair that has to agree in gender and number)
reviewVocab.example: В предложении 'это новые дома' цепочка 'новые-дома' стоит в множественном числе.

reviewVocab.definition: this / these (an invariant pointer; does not change form for gender or number)
reviewVocab.example: В русском языке 'это' остаётся одинаковым: это новый дом, это новые дома, это новая улица.

reviewVocab.definition: the standard A1 Russian way to express 'I have'; the noun stays in the nominative
reviewVocab.example: В предложении 'у меня хорошие друзья' существительное 'друзья' стоит в именительном падеже, а прилагательное согласуется с ним.
